Elena — appreciate the quick review and the legal note. High-level replies inline below; attaching our checklist and a draft escalation matrix so we can align on concrete acceptance gates.

- Productization Title: Redwood's standard position is that customers retain title to customer-provided content and derivative outputs used solely in their application. If we perform model retraining that incorporates customer data for general model improvement, we request a limited feedback license. That said, for this deal we can propose an explicit carve-out: "customer retains exclusive title to model outputs used in the customer's end product; Redwood will not assert ownership over customer outputs generated during the term."

- Evidence pack: we can provide anonymized request/response slices, KV cache traces for sessions (redacted), and a telemetry summary (counts, latencies, token-level aggregates). We do not provide verbatim production logs unless explicitly agreed and covered by a data transfer attestation.

- SLA for telemetry incidents: we can commit to a 24-hour initial acknowledgement and a 72-hour remediation/response window for items requiring engineering changes. For critical PII exposures we will prioritize and escalate to a 8-hour investigation window as an exception.

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick call to confirm checklist items, 2) exchange a final MSA snippet accepting the carve-out language, 3) order form sign-off with the attachments we just shared.

Diego
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Diego / Laura — quick operational request before we lock the language. On NovaProd's side our Compliance team requires a short list of evidence items we can hold the order form against. Proposed minimal set: 

1) Snapshot of sample outputs (redacted) showing no embedded customer PII or copyrighted materials.
2) Telemetry summary covering the first 30 days after go-live (token counts, top error classes, anonymized request patterns).
3) A signed attestation that Redwood will not feed customer outputs into open-model training pipelines or external model improvement programs without explicit opt-in.

If Redwood can commit to those three acceptance items as part of the order form exhibits, we can proceed with signature and procurement.

Tom / Elena — thanks, that's very actionable. Short answers and proposed wording below: 

1) Sample outputs: we will produce a 10-sample redacted evidence pack embedded in Exhibit B. Wording: "Redwood will provide ten representative, redacted sample outputs demonstrating compliance with the customer's data use constraints."

2) Telemetry summary: we commit to deliver a 30-day telemetry report (aggregated metrics only) as an Exhibit. Wording: "Redwood will deliver a telemetry report covering the first 30 days post-go-live that includes aggregate token usage, headroom, and error rate breakdowns; no PII will be disclosed."

3) Attestation on training: proposed clause: "Redwood will not use customer outputs or customer-provided content to improve or train any models outside of the dedicated instance(s) serving the customer unless Customer explicitly opts in via a written amendment."

If that language looks good, we can fold it into the MSA redlines and update Exhibit references in the order form. Marcus, Ben — can you confirm the implementation feasibility for the 10-sample pack and the telemetry export format?

Laura Bennett
